title: The effect of small-ball-based physical activity on multicomponent agility in 11 12 year old students El efecto de la actividad física con pelota pequeña sobre la agilidad multicomponente en estudiantes de 11 a 12 años
abstract: Developing multicomponent agility through school-based activities that integrate multidirectional movement and object manipulation remains an important but insufficiently investigated area in physical education. This study aimed to examine the effect of small-ball-based physical activity on multicomponent agility in students aged 11-12 years and to determine whether the effects differed by initial agility level. This study employed a matched pretest-posttest control-group design with a 2 × 2 treatment-by-level arrangement. A total of 80 students aged 11-12 years participated. The intervention group participated in a small-ball game program for 6 weeks, with 3 sessions per week (18 sessions in total). The program incorporated running, changes of direction, acceleration, deceleration, coordination, accuracy, and rapid responses, while maintaining a controlled intensity of approximately 65%-75% and RPE 12-14. The control group participated in matched free-play physical education activities. Multicomponent agility was assessed using the N-Challenge Test. title: Social representations of the ideal university professor among undergraduate Physical Education students Representaciones Sociales del buen docente universitario en estudiantes de Licenciatura en Educación Física
abstract: The evaluation of university professors has relied predominantly on research performance indicators and science communication metrics, overlooking the subjective perspectives of students and professors themselves regarding what constitutes a good university professor. This study aims to establish the social representations of a good university professor among undergraduate students in Physical Education in Medellín. A sequential mixed-methods design was conducted with 100 undergraduate students selected through simple random sampling, using Natural Semantic Networks. In-depth interviews were carried out with 5 prominent professors and analyzed using Atlas.ti version 25. Differences between groups were assessed according to semester of study (p

title: Educational value of orienteering in higher education physical education: perceptions and experiences of college students Valor educativo de la orientación deportiva en la educación física superior: percepciones y experiencias de estudiantes universitarios
abstract: Orienteering is an outdoor and adventure-based activity that combines navigation, map reading, route planning, and decision-making while promoting physical, cognitive, and social development. Despite its documented educational benefits, its integration into higher education physical education programs in the Philippines remains limited. This study aimed to examine college students' perceptions of orienteering as a component of the Physical Activity Toward Health and Fitness (PATHFit) program in terms of the mechanics of the activity, perceived safety, facilities and equipment, enjoyment, and general acceptability. A descriptive cross-sectional mixed-methods design was employed. The participants consisted of 250 college students enrolled in a state university in the Philippines who had participated in orienteering activities. Data were collected using a validated researcher-developed questionnaire with a reliability coefficient of α = 0.844 and an open-ended survey question. Quantitative data were analyzed using frequency counts, percentages, mean scores, and median values, while qualitative responses were analyzed using thematic analysis. title: Development of fundamental movement skills research in last decade: a systematic review and bibliometric analysis Desarrollo de la investigación sobre habilidades fundamentales del movimiento en la última década: una revisión sistemática y análisis bibliométrico
abstract: This study presents a systematic review and bibliometric analysis of fundamental movement skills (FMS) research over the past decade (2015–2024), explicitly following PRISMA guidelines and utilizing VOSviewer (version 1.6.19) for bibliometric mapping. A total of 611 articles were retrieved from the Scopus database, of which 520 met the inclusion criteria after screening for peer-reviewed English articles with full-text access. The analysis reveals that FMS publications peaked in 2021 (72 articles), yet average citations per article declined sharply from 44.59 in 2015 to 2.27 in 2024. Australia contributed the highest number of publications (127; average citations 29.20), followed by the United Kingdom (103; 17.53) and the United States (62; 28.17), indicating an Anglo-centric dominance in the field. Medicine (338 publications) and Health Professions (197 publications) emerged as the dominant subject areas. The ten most cited studies focused on three core themes: validation of FMS assessment tools, structured interventions in physical education and family settings, and conceptual models linking FMS to lifelong physical activity and injury prevention. title: The relationships among workplace bullying, organizational commitment, and quiet quitting among physical education professionals Las relaciones entre el acoso laboral, el compromiso organizativo y la renuncia silenciosa entre los profesionales de la educación física
abstract: Workplace bullying is a significant organizational risk for sports education institutions. It can deplete employees’ psychological resources and weaken their organizational commitment, which may lead to an increase in quiet quitting. This study examined the levels of workplace bullying, organizational commitment, and quiet quitting among sports education employees. Additionally, the measurement properties of these three constructs and the relationships among them were evaluated. A total of 550 participants took part in this cross-sectional and correlational study. Data were collected using a 39-item, five-point Likert-type scale. There were 13 items in each dimension. Internal consistency was examined using Cronbach’s alpha and McDonald’s omega coefficients. Confirmatory factor analysis based on weighted least squares estimation was conducted to assess construct validity. The mean scores were 2.92 ± 0.71 for workplace bullying, 3.17 ± 0.60 for organizational commitment, and 2.26 ± 0.67 for quiet quitting. The alpha coefficients ranged from 0.913 to 0.932. title: Attitudinal style and basic psychological needs of university students: a qualitative study based on self-determination theory Estilo actitudinal y necesidades psicológicas básicas de los estudiantes universitarios: un estudio cualitativo basado en la teoría de la autodeterminación
abstract: This study adopts an exploratory qualitative design to analyze the effects of the Attitudinal Style emerging pedagogical model, alongside the implementation of self-regulated learning strategies, on the Basic Psychological Needs of university students enrolled in the bachelor’s degree in Human Movement Sciences. The research is framed within Self-Determination Theory, which emphasizes the role of autonomy, competence, and relatedness in motivation and learning. Data were collected using a set of open-ended questions as the primary data collection tool. A total of 76 university students (56 males and 20 females, aged 18 to 23 years) participated in the study. Results suggest that the Attitudinal Style model, through its emphasis on autonomy support and the promotion of self-regulated learning, may enhance students' Basic Psychological Needs, fostering a more inclusive and motivating educational environment

title: Senso-perceptive abilities and motor coordination in 8-9 year old children: evidence from a school-based study Habilidades sensoperceptivas y coordinación motriz en niños de 8 a 9 años: evidencia de un estudio escolar
abstract: Gross motor coordination reflects the integration of sensori-motor processes, including visual-spatial orientation and proprioceptive feedback, which are essential for efficient movement execution during childhood. Disruptions in this integration may restrict participation in physical activity and adversely affect quality of life. The purpose of this study was to evaluate gross motor coordination in children aged 8-9 years and to examine potential gender-related differences in motor performance. A total of 145 children (74 boys and 71 girls) from public primary schools in the urban area of Shkodra, Albania, participated in the study. Gross motor coordination was assessed using the Körperkoordinationstest für Kinder (KTK), which includes the Backward Walking, Hopping for Height (Right and Left leg), Lateral Jumps, and Platform Shifting. Descriptive and inferential statistical analyses were conducted. Boys demonstrated significantly higher performance in Hopping Right (p = .039) and Platform Shifting (p = .032), whereas girls performed significantly better in Backward Walking (p = .026). title: Policy implementation and challenges in sports development programs: a qualitative systematic review and thematic synthesis Implementación de políticas en programas de desarrollo deportivo: revisión sistemática cualitativa y síntesis temática
abstract: Sports development programs (SDPs) aim to facilitate meaningful participation in sport, but their effectiveness depends not only on policy design but also on implementation and stakeholder experiences. This qualitative systematic review and thematic synthesis examined stakeholders’ perspectives on policy implementation in SDPs across diverse international contexts. Following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines, searches of Scopus, PubMed, and Google Scholar identified eligible qualitative and mixed-method studies published in English between 2020 and 2025. Twenty-five studies were included and appraised using the Critical Appraisal Skills Programme (CASP) Qualitative Checklist, and findings were synthesized using thematic synthesis. Five analytical themes emerged: (1) governance and financial pressures; (2) policy–practice gaps; (3) structural and capacity constraints; (4) power and inequality; and (5) cultural and motivational challenges. title: Evaluating FunEBall in physical education: an explanatory sequential mixed methods study Evaluación de FunEBall en educación física: un estudio de métodos mixtos secuencial explicativo
abstract: FunEBall is an inclusive net-based team sport designed to promote cooperation, active participation, and enjoyment. This study evaluated its implementation in university physical education using an explanatory sequential mixed-methods design. In the quantitative phase, 60 students from a state university in Davao Oriental, Philippines, were selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected using the researcher-developed FunEBall Student Feedback Survey and analyzed using descriptive statistics, independent-samples t-tests, ANOVA, Tukey's HSD test, supplementary nonparametric analyses (Mann–Whitney U and Kruskal–Wallis H tests), effect size measures, and Cronbach's alpha. In the qualitative phase, open-ended responses were analyzed using thematic analysis. Results indicated that students reported very positive perceptions of FunEBall across the dimensions of engagement and participation, learning outcomes, physical activity and fitness, and enjoyment and perception. title: Adaptabilidad motriz mediante aprendizaje basado en retos motrices en escolares de seis años Motor adaptability through motor challenge-based learning in six-year-old schoolchildren
abstract: Ecuadorian Physical Education requires pedagogical approaches that foster motor adaptability; however, traditional technique-centered methods continue to predominate, limiting the integration of motor, cognitive, emotional, and social development in young learners. The aim of this study was to determine the effect of the Motor Challenge-Based Learning Model (MCBLM) on motor adaptability among six-year-old students enrolled in private educational institutions in Quito, Ecuador, during the second academic term of the 2025–2026 school year. A quantitative quasi-experimental design was employed with a sample of 282 six-year-old students. The experimental group received twelve Physical Education sessions structured according to the MCBLM, while the control group followed a traditional instructional approach. Motor adaptability was assessed using the Motor Adaptability Observation Scale for Six-Year-Old Students (EOAM-6). The experimental group improved from 11.39 to 15.47 points (Δ = +4.08), whereas the control group increased from 11.29 to 12.59 points (Δ = +1.30). title: La práctica del Goalball como ocupación significativa: identidad, espiritualidad y significado en personas con discapacidad visual Goalball as a meaningful activity: identity, spirituality, and meaning among people with visual impairments
abstract: Goalball, a Paralympic sport designed for people with visual impairments, has been studied mainly for its physical and social benefits, with little attention to subjective dimensions such as occupational identity, spirituality, beliefs, and values. This qualitative research, framed within the interpretive paradigm, analyzed the experiences of five athletes from the Biobío Region (Chile) through semi-structured interviews and thematic analysis. The results show that the practice of Goalball operates as a meaningful occupation that transforms limiting beliefs —moving from discouragement to autonomy and self-efficacy—, promotes values such as empathy, respect, cooperation, and resilience, and channels spiritual dimensions linked to life purpose and mental strength. Furthermore, the sport contributes to the construction of a positive occupational identity, acting as a mirror of personal and collective growth. However, structural tensions persist: discontinuity of public policies, political instrumentalization of disability, and a gap between the inclusive sports environment and other social contexts that limit the transfer of learning. title: Barreras y facilitadores de la adherencia al fútbol recreativo en adolescentes varones con riesgo cardiometabólico: un estudio cualitativo derivado de un ECA Barriers and facilitators of adherence to recreational football in adolescents with cardiometabolic risk: a qualitative study derived from an RCT
abstract: Adherence to physical exercise programs among adolescents with cardiometabolic risk is a complex phenomenon linked to individual, social, and contextual experiences. The aim of this study was to understand the experiences of adolescents with cardiometabolic risk who participated in two recreational football modalities, identifying barriers and facilitators associated with adherence or dropout. A qualitative interpretive study was conducted with 17 male adolescents aged 11 to 15 years who participated in a randomized controlled trial comparing two football training modalities designed to promote cardiometabolic health. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with seven adolescents who dropped out of the program or showed low adherence, and focus groups were conducted with ten highly adherent participants. Reflexive thematic analysis was carried out by the research team through an inductive, iterative, and reflexive process, strengthened by a systematic record of analytical decisions and critical discussions among researchers, which enabled the construction of three central themes. title: Organizational components and athlete participation in university team sports: A systems-based analysis Componentes organizacionales y participación de atletas en deportes colectivos universitarios: un análisis basado en sistemas
abstract: Collegiate sports programs rely on coordinated organizational support to sustain athlete participation across competitive levels. This study examined the implementation of four organizational components of a university Sports Development Program and their relationships with athlete participation among collegiate varsity student-athletes. A quantitative cross-sectional explanatory design was employed with 75 varsity student-athletes from basketball, volleyball, baseball, and softball at a public university in the Philippines. Data were collected using a researcher-developed 70-item questionnaire assessing recruitment and retention, benefits and incentives, sports facilities, equipment maintenance, and participation in local, regional, and national competitions. Descriptive statistics, Pearson product–moment correlation, and multiple linear regression were used. The organizational components were generally highly to very highly implemented. Athlete participation was very high at the local and regional levels and high at the national level. title: Association between university athletes' routines and academic performance across different sports within the context of a Brazilian university Asociación entre la rutina de los atletas universitarios y el rendimiento académico en diferentes modalidades deportivas en el contexto de una universidad Brasileña
abstract: Sports-academic reconciliation can be understood as the process through which athletes seek to combine their athletic routines with their educational paths. This study aimed to identify the association between the routines of university athletes and their academic performance across different sports. A quantitative, descriptive, and correlational cross-sectional design was adopted. A validated questionnaire was administered to 135 student-athletes. Descriptive and inferential analyses were conducted, including Spearman’s correlation and the Kruskal–Wallis test. The results indicated that the Academic Performance Index showed no statistically significant association with the investigated variables, including academic period (ρ = 0.098, p = 0.265), commuting time (ρ = 0.050, p = 0.570), weekly leisure time (ρ = 0.028, p = 0.751), sleep time (ρ = 0.049, p = 0.576), and study time (ρ = 0.005, p = 0.956). Furthermore, no statistically significant differences were found in the Academic Performance Index among athletes engaged in individual, team, or both types of sports [H (2) = 1.655, p = 0.437]. title: Development and preliminary validation of a physical education cognitive test across lower-, middle-, and higher-order thinking skills in students aged 12-15 years Desarrollo y validación preliminar de una prueba cognitiva de educación física que evalúa las habilidades de pensamiento de orden inferior, medio y superior en estudiantes de 12 a 15 años
abstract: Physical Education cognitive assessment requires validated instruments that capture not only factual knowledge but also students’ ability to apply and evaluate concepts in movement-related contexts. This study aims to develop and conduct a preliminary validation of a Physical Education cognitive test based on Lower-Order Thinking Skills (LOTS), Middle-Order Thinking Skills (MOTS) and Higher-Order Thinking Skills (HOTS) for students aged 12-15 years. This study employed a quantitative approach in the development and preliminary validation of the instrument. Content validation involved nine validators, comprising four lecturers and five Physical Education teachers from pilot schools. The empirical pilot study involved 722 students who returned complete and codable answer sheets in grades 7, 8 and 9 from five junior high schools. The instrument developed comprises 47 LOTS items, 35 MOTS items and 33 HOTS items, each with four answer options. The topics covered include big ball games, small ball games, athletics, gymnastics, physical fitness, pencak silat, healthy lifestyles and injury prevention. title: Estudio de caso de la formación inicial docente en Educación Física en una universidad en Chile Case Study on Initial Teacher Training in Physical Education at a University in Chile
abstract: Initial Teacher Education (ITE) in Physical Education is facing global and local changes in Chile as it seeks to meet the demands of an increasingly heterogeneous educational system. The objective of this study was to reveal the structural coherence between the graduate profile, the educational pathway, and the perceptions of teacher educators and fifth-year students. A qualitative methodological approach was adopted within a descriptive-interpretive case study design. Through purposive sampling, 6 students in professional practicum and 5 faculty members participated. The techniques employed included focus groups, semi-structured interviews, and document analysis, ensuring ethical safeguards such as informed consent, anonymity, and voluntary participation. Data processing was conducted using deductive-inductive thematic analysis in ATLAS.ti, employing coding and methodological triangulation. The results reveal a tension stemming from an imbalance in the training curriculum, which prioritizes a biological-sports-oriented approach over a comprehensive pedagogical one. title: Work engagement and burnout among public school physical education teachers in the Philippines: The predictive role of absorption Compromiso laboral y agotamiento entre los profesores de educación física de escuelas públicas en Filipinas: El papel predictivo de la absorción
abstract: This study examined work engagement and burnout among public school physical education teachers in the DepEd Davao del Norte Division, Philippines. Specifically, it determined the level of work engagement, the level of burnout, the relationship between work engagement and burnout, and the work engagement dimensions that significantly predict burnout. The study used a quantitative, cross-sectional, descriptive-correlational design with regression analysis. Participants were 141 full-time public school physical education teachers, representing the total eligible population in the division. Data were collected using adapted questionnaires on work engagement and burnout and were analyzed using mean, standard deviation, Pearson product-moment correlation, and multiple linear regression. Results showed that the respondents reported a high overall level of work engagement (M = 4.19, SD = 0.44), with dedication obtaining the highest mean (M = 4.27, SD = 0.58). Burnout was moderate overall (M = 3.29, SD = 0.56), with personal accomplishment obtaining the highest mean (M = 4.26, SD = 0.74), followed by exhaustion (M = 3.19, SD = 0.84), while depersonalization was low (M = 2.44, SD = 0.86). title: Mindset, resilience, and future career orientation in young professional badminton athletes: implications for dual career development Actitud mental, resiliencia y orientación profesional futura en jóvenes deportistas profesionales de bádminton: implicaciones para el desarrollo de una doble carrera
abstract: Athletes’ psychological readiness is essential not only for performance development but also for successful career transitions beyond sport. However, many young athletes tend to prioritize performance outcomes over long-term career planning. This study aimed to examine the mindset, resilience, and future career orientation of young professional badminton athletes within the context of dual career development. A descriptive quantitative design was employed involving 19 athletes selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire based on Growth Mindset Theory, Social Cognitive Career Theory (SCCT), and the Health Action Process Approach (HAPA). The instrument consisted of 25 dichotomous items (Yes/No) with good reliability (KR-20 = 0.82). Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics (frequency and percentage). The findings suggested high levels of growth mindset (96.0%) and resilience and self-regulation (95.0%) among the participating athletes, indicating strong persistence and adaptive learning behaviors. title: Adaptación y validación del cuestionario CONACT-SVB de conocimientos y actitudes sobre soporte vital básico en Educación Secundaria Adaptation and validation of the CONACT-SVB questionnaire of knowledge and attitudes on basic life support in Secondary Education
abstract: Basic Life Support (BLS) training in schools is crucial for improving bystander response to out-of-hospital cardiac arrest. This study culturally adapted, expanded, and psychometrically validated a questionnaire to assess knowledge, attitudes, self-confidence, motivation, and intention regarding BLS performance and the use of an automated external defibrillator (AED) among secondary school students in Spain. A total of 317 secondary school students participated. The questionnaire included 15 multiple-choice items on knowledge and 16 on attitudes. Difficulty and discrimination indices were calculated for the knowledge items, while the attitude scale was analyzed using exploratory (EFA) and confirmatory (CFA) factor analysis. Internal consistency (Cronbach’s alpha and McDonald’s omega) and measurement invariance based on sex, educational level, and prior BLS/AED training were evaluated. title: Integrated framework for holistic student development: physical literacy, nutrition, and playground design in ASEAN Marco integrado para el desarrollo integral del alumno: alfabetización física, nutrición y diseño de patios de recreo en la ASEAN
abstract: Holistic student development in ASEAN (Association of Southeast Asian Nations) educational contexts demands integrated approaches that simultaneously address physical literacy, nutrition literacy, and supportive play environments. This study aimed to develop and empirically validate an integrated physical literacy, nutrition literacy, and playground-based framework. A four-phase sequential mixed-methods design was applied, including expert consultation, document analysis, prototype development, and quantitative validation. Construct validation involved 1415 elementary students and was analyzed using descriptive statistics, correlation, regression, and structural equation modeling. Students demonstrated high levels of holistic development (M = 78.2), physical literacy (M = 76.4), creativity in play (M = 74.3), and nutrition literacy (M = 72.1), with daily physical activity showing moderate levels (M = 68.9). title: Development of an eight-shaped field test for aerobic capacity assessment in wheelchair basketball: a pilot study Desarrollo de una prueba de campo en ocho para evaluar la capacidad aeróbica en baloncesto en silla de ruedas: estudio piloto
abstract: Wheelchair basketball (WB) requires sport-specific assessment procedures that reflect the propulsion and turning demands of on-court performance. Traditional shuttle-based field tests may not fully reproduce the movement patterns of WB, particularly regarding bidirectional turns and continuous wheelchair propulsion. This pilot study aimed to develop and describe a novel eight-shaped field-test protocol designed to better reflect WB-specific propulsion and turning demands, and to explore its feasibility and preliminary cardiorespiratory responses compared with a laboratory treadmill protocol. Two male WB athletes with different functional classifications (1.0 and 3.0) completed a maximal incremental treadmill protocol and the proposed on-court test, both performed with Oxycon Jaeger® metabolic gas analysers. VO2max values reached during the field test were lower than those recorded in the laboratory for both participants (38.6 vs. 44.42 mL/kg/min for class 3.0; 32.35 vs. 38.33 mL/kg/min for class 1.0). title: Perturbation-based vs multicomponent training in adults over 70: effects on balance and mobility Entrenamiento con perturbaciones vs multicomponente en mayores de 70: equilibrio y movilidad
abstract: Traditional multicomponent exercise programs generally focus on proactive balance control, whereas perturbation-based training aims to improve reactive responses to unexpected destabilizing events. The aim of this study was to compare the effects of a perturbation-based multicomponent exercise program with those of a traditional multicomponent program on strength, balance, and functional mobility in community-dwelling women aged over 70 years. Sixty-one women were randomly allocated to a perturbation-based training group (PT; n = 32) or a traditional multicomponent training group (MT; n = 29). Both groups completed an eight-week intervention consisting of two weekly sessions lasting 45 minutes. In the PT group, the central phase of each session included progressively challenging perturbation tasks characterized by increasing environmental unpredictability and sensory constraints, whereas the MT group performed light-to-moderate multicomponent exercises without systematic perturbations. Physical performance was assessed before and after the intervention using functional tests related to strength, balance, and mobility. title: ¿Distribución desigual? Brechas en el financiamiento del deporte adaptado en Chile: el caso de un fondo público Unequal Distribution? Gaps in the funding of adapted sport in Chile: the case of a public fund
abstract: Despite regulatory progress in the field of inclusion, Adapted Sport remains one of the most underfunded areas within state financing. This study aims to analyze the distribution of public resources allocated to Adapted Sport in the Biobío Region of Chile, through the analysis of a regional competitive sports fund during the period 2015–2023. A quantitative, descriptive, and documentary approach was applied, with a non-experimental, longitudinal, and retrospective design. A total of 3559 projects financed by the Regional Government of Biobío through the FNDR-Sports program were analyzed. The results indicate that 98% of the initiatives were implemented by private entities and that, until 2019, the budget allocated to Adapted Sport was below 1% of the total annual funding, increasing to 5.5% in 2020. The competitive area concentrated 66.1% of the total resources, while the formative and recreational areas accounted for 13.6% and 18.2%, respectively. The disciplines of Wheelchair Basketball and Boccia represented 62% of the initiatives and 62.9% of the total funding. title: The mediating role of sports self-confidence in the relationship between sports anxiety and perceived sports performance of suc-3 student-athletes during the in-season El papel mediador de la autoconfianza deportiva en la relación entre la ansiedad deportiva y el rendimiento deportivo percibido de atletas universitarios SUC-3 durante la temporada
abstract: Competitive sport environments expose athletes to psychological pressures that influence performance, particularly through the interaction of sports anxiety and sports self-confidence. Understanding these dynamics during the in-season is critical for optimizing athlete outcomes and performance consistency. This study aimed to determine the levels of sports anxiety, sports self-confidence, and perceived sports performance; examine sex differences; and test the direct and mediating relationships among these variables. A quantitative cross-sectional correlational–mediation design was employed involving 106 collegiate student-athletes (61 females, 45 males). Data were collected using standardized instruments and analyzed using regression-based mediation analysis with the Sobel test.Results indicated that athletes exhibited varying levels of sports anxiety, sports self-confidence, and perceived sports performance. Significant sex differences were observed, with females reporting higher cognitive anxiety (M = 3.27, SD = 0.60) than males (M = 2.76, SD = 0.81; p = .001). title: Physical literacy in Primary Physical Education: A systematic review of game-centred, outdoor, and digitally supported pedagogy Alfabetización física en Educación Física en Primaria: una revisión sistemática de pedagogías centradas en el juego, al aire libre y apoyadas digitalmente
abstract: Primary physical education (PE) is an important context for developing physical literacy (PL), which integrates motivation, confidence, physical competence, knowledge, and understanding to support lifelong engagement in physical activity. This systematic review synthesized evidence published from 2020 to 2025 on pedagogical models, design principles, and implementation conditions associated with PL outcomes in primary PE. Using a PRISMA-informed method, studies from Scopus and Web of Science were screened, and 23 articles were included. Four themes emerged. First, hybrid pedagogical models, including game-centred approaches combined with Sport Education, TGfU, or Cooperative Learning, supported enjoyment, tactical learning, and social development. Second, autonomy support, inclusive differentiation, formative assessment, representative tasks, and progressive complexity were the most consistent design principles. Third, the more consistent evidence indicated improvements in competence-related outcomes, including fitness and skill development, while validated game-based observation strengthened authentic assessment. title: Global Evolution of Research on Plyometric Training for Improving Lower-Limb Muscle Strength and Power: A Systematic Review and Bibliometric Evolución global de la investigación sobre el entrenamiento pliométrico en la mejora de la fuerza y la potencia muscular de las extremidades inferiores: revisión sistemática y análisis bibliométrico
abstract: This paper describes the global development of literature about plyometric exercise with the purpose of improving the strength and explosive force of the lower limbs. A combined systematic review with bibliometric analysis was carried out in the literature of Scopus, PubMed, and ScienceDirect databases for the period of 2001-2025. The PRISMA-2020 protocol guided the systematic review procedure. A total of 14 experimental and quasi-experimental studies were selected for the systematic review, together with 784 articles analyzed in the bibliometric analysis with VOS_viewer. The outcome of the analysis showed an increased rate of published literature after the year 2017, particularly among authors from Europe and authors from Oceania, with an emphasis changing from mechanism-oriented studies towards performance-related studies. With the literature analysis of improvements in force, speed, and functionality of the lower limbs of varying ages and sports situations, it can accordingly be concluded that the literature about plyometric exercise has indeed developed extensively around the globe with explicit efficiency while emphasizing new studies about optimal dosages.

title: Relación entre el excesivo uso del smartphone, el nivel de actividad física con el sobrepeso y obesidad en adolescentes The relationship between excessive smartphone use, physical activity levels, and overweight and obesity in adolescents
abstract: Excessive smartphone use has increased dramatically worldwide among adolescents, leading to a sedentary lifestyle, physical inactivity, overweight, and obesity. The objective was to determine the relationship between excessive smartphone use, physical activity levels, and overweight and obesity among adolescents in Juliaca, Peru, in 2025. Materials and methods: A non-experimental study with a descriptive correlational design was conducted. A non-probabilistic sample of 827 adolescents aged 12 to 17 years (425 females and 402 males) from public schools was selected. The instruments used were questionnaires on time spent on smartphones and physical activity, which were validated by experts and obtained a Cronbach’s alpha of 0.91 and 0.87, respectively. Anthropometric measurements of body weight and height were taken. Results: 35.3% and 27.7% spend 3 to 4 and 5 to 6 hours daily, respectively, on smartphones during the week. Regarding physical activity, females showed a low level (17.2%), in contrast to males, who showed a high level (15.5%). Regarding BMI, adolescents had a normal level (56.1%), while females showed a prevalence of overweight and obesity (15.6% and 9.8%, respectively)

title: When masculinity polices the body: body image as a mediator of dance self-efficacy among university students Cuando la masculinidad regula el cuerpo: la imagen corporal como mediadora de la autoeficacia en danza entre estudiantes universitarios
abstract: Dance participation in higher education supports physical, psychological, and social development; however, gendered norms may constrain male students’ engagement and confidence in expressive movement contexts. Rigid masculine expectations may shape how male bodies are perceived and performed, potentially influencing both body-related perceptions and dance self-efficacy. This study examined whether body image mediates the relationship between toxic masculinity and dance self-efficacy among Filipino male university students. A quantitative cross-sectional mediation design was employed with 104 male undergraduate students enrolled in PATHFIT dance-related courses. Data were collected using the Toxic Masculinity Scale (TMS), Body Appreciation Scale-2 (BAS-2), and Dance Self-Efficacy Scale, and analyzed using PROCESS Model 4 with bootstrapping and the Sobel test. title: Gamificación y Educación Física: beneficios, desafíos y principios. Revisión narrativa. Gamification and Physical Education: benefits, challenges, and principles. A narrative review.
abstract: Contemporary Physical Education faces challenges that demand pedagogical innovation and teaching strategies aligned with current educational needs. In this context, gamification has emerged as a methodological alternative that integrates game elements into non-game environments, promoting motivation, interaction, and active student participation. The aim of this narrative review was to critically analyze the benefits, challenges, and principles associated with the implementation of gamification in Physical Education. A systematized search was conducted in five international databases: Scopus, Web of Science, ERIC, Dialnet y PubMed until November 2025, using Boolean combinations in English and Spanish. Out of 157 identified articles, 20 studies published between 2021 and 2025 were selected, including reviews and empirical research published in indexed journals. The findings indicate that gamification increases motivation, engagement, autonomy, and meaningful learning, while also improving physical performance, teamwork, and classroom climate. Additionally, it strengthens socio-emotional skills, cooperation, and self-regulation, fostering more inclusive and participatory learning env

title: Teaching smart under constraints: lesson pacing, space improvisation, and reflective practice in elementary Physical Education Enseñar de forma inteligente bajo restricciones: ritmo de las lecciones, improvisación espacial y práctica reflexiva en la Educación Física elemental
abstract: This study explored how Filipino Physical Education teachers navigate instructional constraints to optimize student learning, focusing on lesson pacing, space improvisation, and reflective practice. Recognizing the challenges posed by limited facilities, scarce equipment, large class sizes, and diverse student needs, the research aimed to describe the adaptive strategies teachers employ to sustain effective, inclusive, and engaging physical education. A qualitative phenomenology design was utilized to capture the lived experiences of 18 purposively selected PE teachers from urban and rural public schools. Data were collected through a semi-structured interview guide with open-ended questions, validated for clarity and relevance, allowing participants to share in-depth reflections and practical examples of their teaching strategies. Analysis followed Colaizzi’s phenomenological framework, involving identification of significant statements, formulation of meanings, clustering into themes, and integration into an exhaustive description of adaptive teaching practices, with participant verification ensuring credibility. title: Data driven inclusive sports management: a pilot evaluation of information system usability in para-badminton athlete tracking Gestión deportiva inclusiva basada en datos: evaluación de la eficacia de los sistemas de información en el desarrollo de atletas de parabádminton
abstract: Effective data management plays an important role in supporting the development of inclusive sports, including para-badminton. However, the adoption of information technology in disability sports has not been optimal and still tends to lag behind. This study aims to examine a prototype-based system designed to improve the management of inclusive sports, particularly in terms of usability, information accessibility, and the monitoring of training activities as well as athlete performance. The research employed a quantitative approach using a one-group pretest-posttest design, involving 30 coaches and para-badminton athletes selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected through a combination of Likert-scale questionnaires, interviews, and direct observations to gain a comprehensive understanding of user experiences. The collected data were then analyzed using descriptive statistics and paired sample t-tests.. title: Educación física y competencias genéricas en la formación de futuros docentes. Una revisión sistemática entre los años 2015 y 2024 Physical education and generic competencies in future teacher education. A systematic review between 2015 and 2024
abstract: Generic or transversal competences (GTC) have become particularly important in the training of university students and future teachers, above all because of their link to employability. The area of Physical Education (PE), due to its practical and experiential characteristics, is an ideal space for working on these types of skills. The objective of this systematic review was to identify and analyse the most important contributions of the last ten years from the area of PE to the acquisition and development of GTC in Higher Education (HE) in the training of future teachers. Articles from four databases (Web of Science, Scopus, Eric and Dialnet) were reviewed, following the guidelines of the PRISMA statement. Of the 324 articles initially selected, eight met the inclusion criteria and were included in the study corpus of this review. The results demonstrate the importance of GTC for the training of university students, for a more complete and comprehensive education. title: Obesity, physical activity, and diabetes mellitus in Indonesia: findings from IFLS-5 Obesidad, actividad física y diabetes mellitus en Indonesia: resultados del estudio IFLS-5
abstract: Diabetes mellitus is a major global health problem. This study aims to examine the relationship between obesity and diabetes mellitus, while considering physical activity. This study used a cross-sectional design based on secondary data from the IFLS-5. A total of 34,241 respondents aged 15 years and older participated. Obesity was defined using BMI, and physical activity was categorized as low, moderate, and vigorous. Diabetes mellitus was determined using HbA1c measurements and medical diagnoses. Data were analyzed using the chi-square test and multivariable logistic regression, adjusted for confounding variables. title: Socio-economic impacts of micro-sport events: a systematic literature review Impactos socioeconómicos de los micro eventos deportivos: una revisión sistemática
abstract: In recent decades, sport events have increasingly been recognised as tools for economic development, social cohesion, and territorial transformation beyond their competitive dimension. Despite their small scale, micro-sport events have attracted growing attention due to their strong local embeddedness and reliance on existing resources. This study examines their socio-economic impacts within territorial contexts through a systematic literature review. Following PRISMA guidelines, the review synthesises 45 peer-reviewed studies from Web of Science and Scopus. The findings highlight both economic outcomes, including sport tourism and visitor expenditure, alongside social outcomes such as social capital, community cohesion, and residents’ perceptions. Governance, sustainability, and territorial attractiveness also emerge as important dimensions. However, gaps persist, including limited use of integrated frameworks, the predominance of cross-sectional quantitative approaches, and the underrepresentation of Global South contexts. title: Mapping the evolution of marketing research in the global fitness industry: a bibliometric and thematic analysis Mapeando la evolución de la investigación de mercados en la industria global del fitness: un análisis bibliométrico y temático
abstract: This study aims to map the evolution of marketing research in the global fitness industry through bibliometric and thematic analysis. Data were collected from Scopus, ScienceDirect, and PubMed databases, covering the period from 2015 to 2025. A total of 2,462 articles were initially identified, with 1,171 articles meeting the inclusion criteria for analysis, and the top 10 most cited studies selected for in-depth review. The analysis was conducted using VOSviewer to examine publication trends, authorship patterns, country contributions, research domains, and thematic developments. The results indicate a significant and consistent increase in research productivity, growing from 30 publications in 2015 to 230 in 2025, with over 15,000 citations globally. The United States, China, and the United Kingdom dominate scientific contributions, while leading authors such as García-Fernández have played a central role in shaping the field. The dominant research themes include service quality, customer satisfaction, loyalty, digital fitness platforms, and customer behavior. title: Actividad física, sedentarismo y calidad de vida en universitarios: Una revisión narrativa Physical activity, sedentary behavior and quality of life in university students: A narrative review
abstract: Physical Activity (PA) is recognized for its benefits on physical and mental health. In contrast, sedentary behavior is a risk factor for non-communicable chronic diseases and represents a public health problem with direct effects on Health-Related Quality of Life (HRQoL). The growing body of research in this field among university students is dispersed and methodologically heterogeneous, highlighting the need for an updated synthesis. This analytical-documentary narrative review examined the relationship between PA and HRQoL in university students based on scientific publications from 2012 to 2022 in Scopus, SportDiscus, Web of Science, and PubMed. The bibliographic search was based on the PICO strategy. Quantitative studies (including descriptive and cross-sectional designs) were included. A total of 459 articles were identified, of which 8 met the inclusion and quality criteria for in-depth analysis. Findings show that students generally do not meet recommended levels of PA. A large portion of their time is spent in sedentary behaviors, which are associated with lower physical, psychological, and social well-being. title: Effectiveness of game-based physical training on aerobic and anaerobic capacity in volleyball players aged 15-18 years: a randomized controlled trial Eficacia del entrenamiento físico basado en juegos sobre la capacidad aeróbica y anaeróbica en jugadores de voleibol de 15 a 18 años: un ensayo controlado aleatorizado
abstract: Volleyball is an intermittent sport that requires both aerobic and anaerobic capacity; therefore, training approaches should match these physiological demands. This study aimed to analyze the effectiveness of game-based physical training on aerobic and anaerobic endurance in volleyball players aged 15-18 years. The study employed a randomized controlled trial design with a pretest-posttest format involving two groups. A total of 48 volleyball players aged 15-18 years (24 males and 24 females) were randomly assigned to an intervention group (game-based physical training) and a control group (conventional training). The intervention was conducted over 8 weeks (24 sessions) with an intensity of 65-85%. Aerobic endurance was measured using the Yo-Yo Intermittent Recovery Test Level 1 (YYIR1), while anaerobic endurance was assessed using the 10 × 20-meter Repeated Sprint Ability test with Total Sprint Time as the indicator. title: Entrenamiento de fuerza con volante de inercia y determinantes del rendimiento en corredores de larga distancia: revisión narrativa Flywheel resistance training and performance determinants in long-distance runners: A narrative review
abstract: Flywheel resistance training, characterized by its emphasis on eccentric force production, has been supported by the scientific literature as an effective strategy for enhancing muscle power, muscle mass, running speed, and sport-specific performance capacities. Within this context, the aim of this narrative review was to provide an overview of the main determinants of performance in long-distance runners, describe how strength training may contribute to their improvement, and examine the potential role of flywheel resistance training in influencing these determinants based on the available scientific evidence.To this end, a narrative review was conducted using the PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and ScienceDirect databases without date restrictions. Systematic reviews, meta-analyses, observational studies, and experimental studies were considered for inclusion.The available evidence suggests that strength training, particularly programs emphasizing eccentric muscle actions and a high rate of force development, improves running economy and endurance performance without compromising maximal oxygen uptake (VO₂max). title: Physical fitness predictors of skill-specific and match performance in Indian sitting volleyball players: a regression analysis approach Predictores de la condición física del rendimiento específico por habilidad y del rendimiento en competición en jugadores indios de voleibol sentado: un enfoque de análisis de regresión
abstract: Sitting volleyball is a Paralympic sport that relies heavily on upper-body physical fitness for players to perform well. Although the sport is becoming increasingly popular in India, there is little research on how physical fitness affects match outcomes among Indian sitting volleyball players. This study set out to find which physical fitness factors best predict skill-specific and overall match performance, using regression analysis. The research included 82 male players aged 18 to 35, chosen from national competitions. The study measured agility, speed, and endurance, forward and backward speed, handgrip strength, upper-body explosive power, flexibility, and coordination. Skill-specific actions like attack, block, service, and defense, as well as overall match results, were recorded and analyzed. The results showed that flexibility had the strongest positive link with performance. Upper-body explosive power, handgrip strength, and coordination were also important, while agility and speed-related factors had negative correlations. title: Parental support and achievement motivation: the mediating role of training satisfaction among tennis athletes Apoyo parental y motivación para el logro: El papel mediador de la satisfacción con el entrenamiento entre los tenistas
abstract: This study empirically analyzed the relationship between parental support and achievement motivation, and explored the mediating role of training satisfaction among tennis athletes. This study employed a quantitative approach with a descriptive-correlational design. The population consisted of field tennis athletes participating in open tennis tournaments from December 2024 to March 2025. A total sample of 155 athletes was obtained, aged 15-23 years, with 6-10 years of training experience and 5-8 years of athletic experience. Data analysis was conducted using SmartPLS.
